spoken_summary: The minimum tenure at a station is three completed years under JRTP Clause 3.1, and no executive may spend more than an aggregate of ten years in a single city or Geographic Cluster over their whole career under JRTP Clause 4.1.
display_text: ONGC Job Rotation & Transfer Policy (JRTP) Statutory Provisions [1]: Minimum normal station tenure is 3 years (Clause 3.1); career cumulative stay cap in a single city or cluster is 10 years (Clause 4.1).

visual.title: Statutory Policy Provision: Station Tenure Norms & Cumulative Stay Cap

clause.text:
3.1 Minimum Station Tenure: The minimum normal tenure of an executive at any station shall be 3 (three) completed years. Normal rotation of an executive shall be considered upon completion of 3 to 5 years at a work centre. No executive shall ordinarily be displaced prior to completing 3 years, except on administrative exigencies approved by Director (HR).

4.1 Maximum Cumulative Career Stay: No executive shall be permitted to spend more than an aggregate of 10 (ten) years at a single city or designated Geographic Cluster over their entire career in the Corporation.
clause.highlight: aggregate of 10 (ten) years at a single city or designated Geographic Cluster

insights: The minimum tenure at a station is 3 completed years (JRTP Clause 3.1), and no executive may spend more than an aggregate of 10 years in a single city over their whole career (JRTP Clause 4.1).
Rotation is normally considered after 3 to 5 years at a work centre; moving someone before 3 years requires administrative exigency or restructuring approved by Director (HR).
The 10-year cap is cumulative: every historical posting in the same station or cluster is added up irrespective of breaks or in-place promotions (JRTP Clause 4.2).

sources.sql:
-- Answer Key SQL: P1
-- Question: What is the minimum tenure at a station, and the maximum cumulative stay in one city?
-- Type: policy
-- Semantic audit 2026-10-20: old query returned only SUBSTR(text,1,300) = the chunk's metadata header
-- (title / glossary), never the clause body, so the answer key contained no actual rule. Now strips the
-- header and extracts the specific sub-clauses that answer the question (column `provision`).
-- Semantic audit 2026-10-20: Dropped the OR'd J-03 court judgment (B.V. Srihari Rao, disciplinary) that sorted first and filled LIMIT 5,
-- pushing both JRTP clauses out of the result.

WITH c AS (
  SELECT doc_id, clause_ref, heading,
         REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(text,
           r'(?s)^.*?Domain Vocabulary[^\n]*\n', ''),
           r'\\\\192\.168\.4\.1\\e\\Public Enterprises \(2018\)(\\4077PE)+\(Chapter 2\)', ' '),
           r'\d*\s*Chapter 2—Personnel Policies\s*\d*', ' '),
           r'Page \d+ of \d+', ' '),
           r'\s+', ' ') AS body
  FROM `ongc-hr-finance-agent.hrfin_docs.silver_chunks`
  WHERE (doc_id = 'JRTP' AND clause_ref = 'Clause 3.0')
     OR (doc_id = 'JRTP' AND clause_ref = 'Clause 4.0')
)
SELECT doc_id, clause_ref, heading, provision, quote_snippet
FROM (
  SELECT 1 AS seq, doc_id, clause_ref, heading, 'JRTP 3.1-3.2' AS provision, TRIM(REGEXP_EXTRACT(body, r'(3\.1 .*?) 3\.3 ')) AS quote_snippet
  FROM c WHERE doc_id = 'JRTP' AND clause_ref = 'Clause 3.0'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 2 AS seq, doc_id, clause_ref, heading, 'JRTP 4.1-4.2' AS provision, TRIM(REGEXP_EXTRACT(body, r'(4\.1 .*?) 4\.3 ')) AS quote_snippet
  FROM c WHERE doc_id = 'JRTP' AND clause_ref = 'Clause 4.0'
)
ORDER BY seq;
